wikipedia.title: Munroe Island
wikipedia.text:
Munroe Island is an inland island group located at the confluence of Ashtamudi Lake and the Kallada River, in Kollam district, Kerala, South India. It is a group of eight small islets comprising a total area of about 13.4 km2. The island, accessible by road, rail and inland water navigation, is about 25 kilometres (16 mi) from Kollam by road, 38 kilometres (24 mi) north from Paravur, 12 kilometres (7.5 mi) west from Kundara and about 25 kilometres (16 mi) from Karunagapally. As of the 2011 Indian census, the administrative village of Mundrothuruth (which includes nearby small villages as well) has a total population of 9054, consisting of 4318 males and 4736 females. This island is also known as "Sinking Island of Kerala".
The place is named in honour of Resident Colonel John Munro of the former Princely State of Travancore. The islands measure 13.4 square kilometres (5.2 sq mi) in area.

wikipedia.title: Koduvila
wikipedia.text: Koduvila is a village near Ashtamudi Lake in East-Kallada, Kollam district, Kerala, India. It shares a boundary with Munroe Island, and is near Chittumala.

wikipedia.title: West Kallada
wikipedia.text: West Kallada  is a village in Kollam district in the state of Kerala, India.

wikipedia.title: Dutch Church, Munroe Island
wikipedia.text: The Dutch Church in Munroe Island, Kollam is one of the old churches in Kerala. The church was built by the Dutch in 1878. The red brick church on the scenic banks of Lake Ashtamudi is a blend of Dutch-Kerala architecture. The only Christian family in the locality is looking after the affairs of this Church. The annual church festival is conducted with the help of the Hindu population residing in the area. It is a good example for the communal harmony existing in Munroe Island in God's own Country (Kerala).

wikivoyage.title: Kollam
wikivoyage.text:
Kollam (കൊല്ലം Kollaṁ), previously Quilon, is a city in southern Kerala (Keralam), India. West and slightly north of the town some 5 km (3.1 mi) lies a beach, on the north end of which are various European colonial-era relics, including the ruins of a fort and a few churches. There are also some old colonial buildings scattered about the town.


== See ==

 Alumkadavu (26 km from Kollam). Scenic place, with blue green stretches back water, coconut palms, back water cruise, house boats, Ayurvedic treatment centers. 
 Aryankavu (73 km east of Kollam). Pilgrim centre, old trade route for merchants from either sides of western Ghats, famous for shrine of Lord Sastha, fine sculptures and mural paintings. 
 Chavara (14 km north of Kollam on NH47). Famous for the mineral sand and place of Catholic saint Sister Alphonsa. 
 Kalayapuram (34 km from Kollam, on the way to Kottayam from Kottarakara). It is believed that old Kalayan royal family were ruled from this place, hence the name Kalayapuram. 
 Karunagappally (27 km north of Kollam in NH47). Famous mosque and dome of martyrs, a unique pilgrimage center. Old military station of Kayamkulam Rajas. 
 Kottarakkara (27 km northeast of Kollam). Erstwhile capital of Elayadathu Swarupam, a ruling family. Famous for Kath Kali (a dance drama). 
 Kundara (13 km east of Kollam, on the way to Kottarakkara). A prominent place in the area famous for industries. 
 Mannadi (24 km east of Kollam). Famous as the place where Veluthampi Dalawa laid down his life. 
 Mayyanad (10 km south of Kollam). Famous for its shrines and temples. 
 Neendakara (Long Shore) (8 km north of Kollam). Famous for its fisheries industries. 
 Sasthamcotta (19 km from Kollam). Biggest freshwater lake in Kerala. 
 Thenmala, 66 km east of Kollam (on the way to Shencottah, it is also reachable from Thiruvananthapuram). Dam site with dense forest is famous for eco tourism. 
 Sakthikulangara (7 kms from Kollam towards Aleppey side). Where the Ashtamudi lake meets the Arabian Sea. Here you will find a leaning lighthouse, similar to the leaning tower of Pisa. (updated Aug 2022)


=== Thangassery ===
Thangassery is home to 18th-century churches, a lighthouse and remnants of Portuguese and Dutch forts.

1 Infant Jesus Cathedral (Malayalam: ഇൻഫന്റ് ജീസസ് കത്തീഡ്രൽ, Portuguese: Igreja do Bom Jesú) (200m north of the Thangassery Fort intersection, on the right-hand side of the road, behind a house). A vestige of the Portuguese rule of Kollam, established in 1614. (updated Mar 2026)
2 St Thomas Fort (Thangassery Fort) (north end of the harbour). Some limited standing ruins of an old colonial fort. You can see two different sides of the building, the first from the harbour side (where it is visible at some distance), and the second from the opposite side. The site is slightly overgrown so beware of snakes if you venture close. An auto-rickshaw from the Main Road bus stop cost ₹50. Free. (updated Mar 2026)
3 Thangassery Lighthouse. 3-5PM. A modern lighthouse in a historic Christian quarter that is possible to climb in the afternoons. Best to combine with the Thangassery Fort, as the two sites are in easy and shaded walking distance. Small fee. (updated Mar 2026)


== Do ==
 Munroe Island Canoe Tours, Chittumala Rd, Munroe Island (Northeast of Kollum), ☏ +91 904 817 6186, vijimunroe@gmail.com. Vijeesh runs canoe tours which are an excellent way to explore Munroe Island. You get to go places that the house boats can't and will literally be going through the village and get to see life there. He has great English and an excellent personality. Also runs a home stay on the island. Rickshaw ~₹400 from Kollam or local train, contact him via email/phone for train details. ₹300 pp. 


=== Beaches ===
It's basically eating, shopping, and sightseeing. Don't swim in the water as there's a large amount of unprocessed sewerage that goes in to it from locals who crap on the beach.

1 Kollam Beach.  (updated Mar 2026)
2 Thangassery Beach. A fishing harbour. (updated Mar 2026)
